la-palma.intro: La Palma's oldest tree is the Pino de la Virgen in El Paso, a Canary pine put at about 800 years by tree-ring counts and called the oldest known of its species. In Breña Alta, two dragon trees 15 metres tall grow a metre and a half apart and sit on the municipal coat of arms. An unnamed drago stands beside the GR 130 footpath above Las Tricias, and at Fuencaliente the Pino del Consuelo marks the site of the first judicial exhumation of Franco-era victims in Spain.
la-palma.meta_description: La Palma's old trees: the 800-year-old Pino de la Virgen in El Paso, the Dragos Gemelos of Breña Alta, where each stands and how to visit.
la-palma.question_meta: La Palma's oldest tree is the Pino de la Virgen in El Paso, a Canary pine of about 800 years.
la-palma.question_answer: The oldest tree on La Palma is the Pino de la Virgen in El Paso, a Canary pine that tree-ring counts in 1995 and 2004 put at 775 to 825 years old; other sources give up to 900. Diario de Avisos calls it the oldest known Canary pine. The island's best-known dragon trees, the Dragos Gemelos in Breña Alta, are said to be 200 to 250 years old.
la-palma.question_context: The Pino de la Virgen's age comes from tree-ring counts made in 1995 and 2004, which gave 775 to 825 years. Newspapers and lists since have said 800 to 850, and 900, so about 800 is the common figure. It is about 33 metres tall and seven metres round, stands beside the Ermita de la Virgen del Pino on a public street, and was declared a Bien de Interés Cultural in 2014. Dragon trees are harder to date. A drago cannot be aged by DNA, and experts estimate from its branchings and cavities, which is why the Dragos Gemelos carry a range of 200 to 250 years that nobody has tested. They stand in a small public square off the LP-301 in Breña Alta, just south of Santa Cruz de La Palma. The drago on the GR 130 has no recorded age, and neither does the Pino del Consuelo, which matters for what happened beside it in 1936 rather than for its size. The four trees are spread from Garafía in the north-west to Fuencaliente in the south, so they make a drive across the island rather than a walk.

faq.q: What is the oldest tree on La Palma?
faq.a: The Pino de la Virgen in El Paso, a Canary pine that tree-ring counts put at 775 to 825 years old; other sources say 800 to 900. Diario de Avisos calls it the oldest known Canary pine.

In a small square in San Isidro, Breña Alta, just south of Santa Cruz de La Palma, reached by a short corridor from a sharp bend of the LP-301. The land belongs to Breña Alta council and the trees can be visited free.

faq.q: Can you visit the Pino del Consuelo?
faq.a: Yes. It is a free roadside memorial site beside the LP-2 before Los Canarios in Fuencaliente, with a monument and plaque unveiled in August 2025 and parking built by the Cabildo. Excavation nearby has continued, so parts of the slope may be fenced.

lanzarote.intro: Yaiza's church has an ombú at its door, a South American species that seems to have been brought to Lanzarote by an islander returning from the Americas. The Biosphere Reserve's 2025 preliminary inventory of singular trees puts it at more than 120 years old and six metres tall, and it has been in photographs and drawings of the church since at least the early twentieth century. It stands in the public Plaza de los Remedios, free to visit at any hour.
lanzarote.meta_description: The ombú at Yaiza church on Lanzarote: over 120 years old, brought from South America, and in pictures of the church for a century.
lanzarote.question_meta: The ombú at Yaiza's church is over 120 years old by Lanzarote's 2025 inventory of singular trees.
lanzarote.question_answer: One of Lanzarote's old trees is the ombú at the door of the Iglesia de Nuestra Señora de los Remedios in Yaiza, put at more than 120 years old by the Biosphere Reserve's 2025 preliminary inventory of singular trees. Which tree is the island's oldest is not settled; Diario de Lanzarote's report on that inventory also names a tamarisk on Alegranza and a school's araucaria as candidates.
lanzarote.question_context: The ombú's age comes from the Lanzarote Biosphere Reserve's preliminary inventory of singular trees, presented in November 2025, which counts 86 singular trees among 166 elements across the island. It is a preliminary list rather than an official catalogue, and the figure of more than 120 years is an estimate, though old photographs and drawings show the tree at the church door since at least the early twentieth century. The tree is six metres tall, small for a famous tree, and its interest is its story. It is a South American species that seems to have arrived with an islander back from the Americas, many neighbours remember the parish priest resting in its shade, and it was left out when the church was protected as a monument in 1986. It stands in the public Plaza de los Remedios, open at any hour, while the church keeps parish hours. Buses between Arrecife and Playa Blanca pass through Yaiza, and the plaza is a few minutes on foot from the main street.

faq.q: What is the tree in front of Yaiza church?
faq.a: An ombú (Phytolacca dioica), a South American species and Argentina's national tree, at the door of the Iglesia de Nuestra Señora de los Remedios. Lanzarote's 2025 inventory of singular trees puts it at more than 120 years old.

faq.q: Is the Yaiza ombú the oldest tree on Lanzarote?
faq.a: Not as far as anyone has shown. Diario de Lanzarote's report on the 2025 inventory names a tamarisk on Alegranza and a school's araucaria as other candidates, without settling which is oldest.
